source_snapshot.procedure: Says to fill files on all available disks, then mount any SSD at `/dev/file`, run `dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/file bs=1M`, check MD5, reboot and recheck MD5; generic setup clears logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Disks fill with files without errors and file MD5 remains correct after reboot.
source_snapshot.script: Private space-fullness-test; 20 attended and 480 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; recognizes a designated volume and near-full risk but does not define eligible-disk coverage, UUID/mount proof, true full boundary, reserve, reboot manifest or cleanup.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at CRITICAL risk; dedicated non-system filesystem, bounded regular files, reserve, manifests, approved reboot/recovery and cleanup.

old_problem: The literal method is unsafe and non-executable: `/dev/file` is created as a directory and then supplied as dd's output, target selection says both all disks and any SSD, and no system/RAID/data exclusion, filesystem identity, full-boundary semantics, recovery or cleanup exists. Reducing the test to one arbitrary volume or a near-full smoke threshold would lose the plural E1.S coverage and formal fullness objective.
disposition_reason: Resolve Pending and Source Conflict at the Review layer using the approved destructive-storage protections. `All available disks` is preserved as every E1.S filesystem explicitly declared eligible in a signed inventory; OS/boot/EFI/swap/LVM/RAID members, production/valid-data and unknown devices are unavailable by safety definition and must carry exclusion evidence. `Mount any SSD` becomes the per-target step repeated for each eligible member, so it no longer narrows coverage. The invalid `/dev/file` target is replaced by regular files under a UUID-verified dedicated mount. Each filesystem reaches its approved true-full terminal condition sequentially, preserves MD5 plus SHA-256, reboots once under approval, verifies the same UUID and hashes, then performs ledgered cleanup. Exact devices/limits are runtime Project inputs rather than an Engineering Decision.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1754, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, pending/conflict analyses, duplicate identity result, private-script reference and ED-01 through ED-30 rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was reconstructed and directly opened as Functionality row 1760 / Wistron-HW-00393-V003 / 4a9df0a3dee080c6.

The source's plural step and criteria control coverage. Interpreting `any SSD` as the current member within a loop over the signed eligible set preserves every safe E1.S target rather than choosing one representative or filling unrelated/system disks.

Storage safety rules require explicit OS, mount, RAID and valid-data protection. Eligibility is therefore a positive allowlist keyed by device serial/WWN/UUID and mount; every discovered but excluded device needs a reason, and an empty eligible set yields BLOCKED rather than unsafe execution.

`dd` writes a regular file path, not a directory or raw namespace. The Review layer uses an owner-approved mount under a normal mount root and manifest-listed files; `/dev/file`, `/dev/nvme*` outputs and guessed targets are prohibited.

Formal fullness is not replaced by a short smoke test. For an isolated disposable filesystem, the signed terminal oracle distinguishes expected capacity/quota boundary from premature EIO/ENODEV/filesystem/SMART failure and preserves filesystem metadata/recovery requirements.

The original MD5 acceptance remains, while SHA-256 is additive. Per-file byte count/hash, sync/unmount policy, one approved reboot, same-UUID remount and post-reboot hash comparison are mandatory before cleanup.
ED-19 preserves logs, ED-23/ED-24 govern the disruptive reboot, ED-26 forbids automatic refill/reboot retry, and no write, mount, reboot, cleanup or DUT action was executed by this review.

test_case.test_name: E1.S Space-Fullness — all eligible isolated filesystems with reboot integrity
test_case.purpose: For every owner-approved eligible E1.S test filesystem, sequentially validate regular-file writes through the signed full-capacity boundary, preserve the expected terminal condition and storage health, then prove exact file integrity and same-filesystem identity after one approved reboot before controlled cleanup.
required_package: Signed complete storage inventory and eligibility matrix: device serial/WWN/BDF/UUID/filesystem/mount for every E1.S target plus exclusions for OS/root/boot/EFI/swap/LVM/RAID members, production/valid-data and unknown devices

Dedicated disposable test filesystem per eligible disk, approved regular-file namespace, true-full boundary/expected terminal error, filesystem reserve/recovery requirements, file size/count plan and 480-minute timeout semantics
Workload drain, backups, recovery console, filesystem/NVMe health acceptance, one-reboot maintenance approval and stable power
Supported `lsblk`, `findmnt`, `df`, `dd` or approved allocator, `sync`, `md5sum`, `sha256sum`, `nvme-cli` and complete evidence/timeout controller
Reviewed private-script revision or equivalent procedure, immutable manifest/evidence path and exact cleanup authorization/ledger
test_case.test_command: APPROVAL-GATED; no DUT action in review. Enumerate storage and fail closed unless the signed allowlist proves each eligible UUID is a mounted disposable E1.S filesystem and every other device is excluded. Sequentially for each eligible member: capture baseline identity/capacity/filesystem/NVMe health; create uniquely named regular files only inside its approved mount, with bounded commands/timeouts and continuous free-space/error monitoring, until the signed true-full terminal condition is reached; treat the expected capacity boundary separately from premature I/O/media errors; record byte counts, MD5 and SHA-256 manifest, sync per approved policy and stop writes. After all target evidence is secure, perform one approved reboot, prove the same UUID/mounts, recompute hashes and health, then remove only manifest-listed files after evidence-owner authorization and verify restored space. Never use `/dev/file`, raw block output, system/RAID/data volumes, unbounded all-disk parallel writes or log clearing.
test_case.expected_result: Every signed eligible E1.S filesystem independently accepts regular-file writes without premature I/O/media/filesystem error until its approved capacity boundary, reaches the exact signed full-state oracle, preserves required metadata/recovery reserve and remains healthy. After the single approved reboot, each same UUID remounts as specified and every manifest-listed file matches both original MD5 and SHA-256. Cleanup removes only test files and restores expected free space; excluded devices, system services and valid data remain unchanged.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete coverage of all allowlisted eligible E1.S filesystems and explicit exclusion evidence for all other discovered disks, plus per-target baseline→full-boundary→reboot→same-UUID/hash→cleanup proof. One representative SSD, near-full smoke percentage, successful dd start, missing expected boundary, raw-device write or post-reboot MD5 without identity/byte count is insufficient. Premature EIO/ENODEV, media/SMART/filesystem error, wrong target, reserve/recovery breach, hash mismatch, mount/reboot failure or incomplete cleanup is reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. The end user decides the verdict.
safety_gate: Never write unless device serial/WWN/UUID/mount is on the signed positive allowlist and independently proven not to be OS/root/boot/EFI/swap/LVM/RAID member, production or valid-data storage.
Use regular files only under the verified test mount; prohibit `/dev/file`, `/dev/nvme*` output, raw devices, guessed mounts and simultaneous unbounded filling.
Execute sequentially with bounded timeout, continuous reserve/health monitoring, stable power, workload drain, backups and recovery console; stop on any premature error or identity drift.
Preserve logs and the first failure; never automatically refill, remount, fsck, reboot again, power-cycle or retry to obtain matching hashes.
Delete only manifest-listed test files after post-reboot evidence authorization; no wildcard/broad cleanup or unrelated data removal.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/Variant, signed complete device eligibility/exclusion matrix and reviewed script/procedure revision
Per-target serial/WWN/BDF/UUID/filesystem/mount identity, baseline capacity/health, workload/backup/recovery/reboot approval and timestamps
Complete fill commands/output, byte counts, free-space/terminal-condition timeline, filesystem/NVMe health and pre-reboot MD5/SHA-256 manifest
Single reboot timeline, same-UUID remount proof, post-reboot dual-hash comparison and preserved SEL/dmesg/syslog
Exact cleanup ledger/restored space, no-system/raw/RAID/data-write and no-retry audit, exceptions and engineer-owned verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong identity, reserve breach, premature ENOSPC/EIO/ENODEV, media/SMART/filesystem issue, mount loss, reboot failure or hash mismatch, stop all writes, preserve the manifest/log/health state and do not retry, fsck, remount or power-cycle automatically. The storage owner invokes the pre-approved UUID-specific recovery using the console/backups. Cleanup occurs only after evidence capture and owner authorization, removing exact manifest entries one target at a time.

source_conflict.reason: Plural all-disk coverage and singular `any SSD` are reconciled without loss: the singular mount/write step repeats sequentially for every positively allowlisted eligible E1.S test filesystem; protected/unknown disks are unavailable and documented exclusions.

blocked.reason: Core write semantics, scope algorithm, terminal oracle classes, evidence and recovery are defined. Exact device allowlist, filesystem boundary and maintenance values are runtime Project configuration; an absent safe target becomes an execution BLOCKED result, not a review ambiguity.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Signed device allowlist/exclusion matrix; UUID mounts; disposable filesystem and true-full terminal/reserve policy; per-file plan/480-minute semantics; health criteria; workload/backup/recovery/reboot approval; private script revision or replacement; cleanup ledger/authorization.
pending.execution_status: REVIEW RESOLVED; EXECUTION NOT STARTED; NO DD/FALLOCATE/WRITE, MOUNT, REBOOT, CLEANUP, LOG CLEAR, NVME/DUT OR OTHER HARDWARE ACTION AUTHORIZED OR EXECUTED

project_authority: The storage/platform owner signs the complete eligible/excluded device matrix, per-filesystem full boundary, reserve, health, reboot and recovery/cleanup plan. The workload owner approves drain/backup/downtime; the evidence owner authorizes cleanup only after verification; the end user decides verdict. AI may not choose a disk or execute the write/reboot.
